criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear goal, four quantified objectives, users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) tied explicitly to needs, and literature cited throughout. Only minor gap: no explicit requirements table with verifiable thresholds beyond the objectives.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef
Its customers are the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority, which needs up-to-date bleaching maps

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt chart with task descriptions, explicit logic linking plan order to mission dependencies, a float week, and a risk/contingency table. Information sources tabulated with planned use. Very robust.

evidence.quote: Project work is divided into weeks in the Gantt chart in Figure 1

criteria.reasoning: Completed background research, STK tutorials, and correct hand calculations (period, SSO inclination, ground-track shift all check out) plus interpretation of the swath/coverage trade and an initial STK scenario. Strong, on-track progress.

evidence.quote: Weekly coverage (objective 1) is therefore not guaranteed by one satellite at this altitude and resolution.

criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, clear writing, labelled figures/tables with captions, consistent IEEE-style citations matching the reference list. Minor issues: some references lack titles/complete details, and reference [11] is a weak source.

technical_issues.issue: Ground-track shift quoted at the equator (24.2°) but reef is at ~18–20°S where tracks converge; the five-pass coverage conclusion is conservative but the reasoning should note latitude scaling.
References [8] and [11] lack full titles/authors; [11] (ResearchGate) is a low-quality source.

overall: Excellent preliminary report: well-justified Australian reef-monitoring mission, quantified objectives, robust Gantt plan with contingencies, correct orbit calculations, and consistent presentation. Minor referencing and latitude-scaling caveats only.

feedback.summary: Excellent preliminary report. Your reef-monitoring mission concept is well justified with quantified objectives and clearly identified users, your Gantt plan is robust with contingencies, and your orbit hand calculations and STK setup show strong progress. Presentation is consistent and professional. To reach the top of each rubric band, add verifiable requirements, note latitude scaling in your ground-track reasoning, and complete your reference details.
next_steps: Add a requirements table with verifiable thresholds (e.g., revisit time, resolution, swath) linked to each objective, so mission requirements are explicitly testable rather than implied by the objectives.

In Preliminary Progress, note that the 24.2° equatorial ground-track shift scales with latitude; discuss coverage at the reef's ~18–20°S latitude where tracks converge, and revisit the five-pass conclusion accordingly.
Complete references [8] and [11] with full titles and authors, and replace the ResearchGate source [11] with a higher-quality primary source.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your mission goal, four quantified objectives, and user needs (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) are clearly linked and well referenced. To fully secure the top level, add an explicit requirements table with verifiable thresholds beyond the objectives themselves.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (9/10). Your Gantt chart (Figure 1) is detailed with task logic, a float week, and a risk/contingency table, and Table 2 tabulates information sources with planned use. The plan clearly fits the mission narrative. Little is missing; consider deepening contingency triggers for schedule slips.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (8/10). Your hand calculations (period, SSO inclination, ground-track shift) are correct and interpreted, and your initial STK scenario shows real progress. Strengthen the coverage analysis by addressing latitude scaling of the ground-track shift at the reef's latitude.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (9/10). Your structure is logical, writing is clear, figures and tables are labelled with captions, and IEEE citations match the reference list. Fix the incomplete details in references [8] and [11] and the weak ResearchGate source to reach full marks.
